new_statements.quote: Nevertheless, multi-syllable words always have a syllable with higher prominence, in terms of intensity, length and clarity. The rules for stress assignment are automatic, and there are no minimal pairs distinguishing words by stress pattern. Both heavy (tone-bearing) and light syllables (tone-less) can bear the word stress. The general rule is that the first heavy syllable in the word is stressed, e.g. ʧì-muɛ̃̀-la [ˈʧiːmuɛ̃la] and not † [ʧiːˈmuɛ̃la]. If a word has one or more short prefixes (which occurs very frequently), the stress moves to the right to the first heavy syllable, e.g. akəʧeì a-kə-ʧei ‘chin’ (V-V-ˈVː). If there is no heavy syllable in the word, but at least two syllables in total, then the first syllable is stressed, e.g. ʤi-la [ˈʤila] conj.

new_statements.rule_in_words: IN BULU (WESTERN) PUROIK, NOT THE TARGET VARIETY: word stress is predictable and non-contrastive; it falls on the leftmost heavy syllable (heavy = has a coda or long vowel/diphthong and bears one of two lexical tones); toneless light prefixes are skipped; a word with no heavy syllable stresses its first syllable; an isolated light monosyllable is lengthened, stressed and gets low tone. The language is also tonal (two tones, high/low, on heavy syllables; neutralised to high before glottal coda).
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not described; author notes 'interaction of tone and stress, realisation of several tones within one word' as open questions (p. 73-74).
new_statements.exceptions: The prefix hã-/ha- 'is unlike other prefixes always stressed' (thesis text line ~3451); stress-tone interaction 'requires further research'.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the phonological word (section 2.6 'Phonological word'); examples are citation forms and prefixed/compounded words. CAVEAT: this statement is first-hand but for Bulu Puroik = Glottolog Western Puroik west2873 (dialect bulu1255), which Lieberherr (2015: 236; 2017: 35) says is not mutually intelligible with the eastern (Chayangtajo / Tibet-side) varieties that constitute sulu1241. For sulu1241 itself the only accessible prosodic statement is second-hand: Sun 1992: 80 reports the ZMYYC Sulong variety has 'a rudimentary system of tones.. two pitch registers' and says nothing about stress; Tayeng 1990 (Chayangtajo) is silent on both stress and tone.
new_statements.identity_note: The quoted stress statement (Lieberherr 2017) describes Bulu Puroik = Glottolog Western Puroik west2873 (dialect Bulu bulu1255), a sister language that Glottolog 5.1 separates from Eastern Puroik sulu1241 and that Lieberherr reports is not mutually intelligible with the eastern varieties; under ISO 639-3 both fall under suv 'Puroik'. It should be credited to west2873 (itself a our source list item whose scan had not found the thesis; the PDF is now.). Sources actually describing sulu1241 varieties: Tayeng 1990 and Remsangpuia 2008 (Chayangtajo, bugu1245), Li 2004/2005 and Sun et al. 1991 (Longzi County Tibet variety, which Lieberherr links to Chayangtajo/Kurung Kumey). Sun 1992 (second-hand) characterises that eastern variety as tonal (two pitch registers).

sources.note: Sec. 2.6.1 'Stress' (pp. 72-73): stress is automatic/non-contrastive; the first heavy (tone-bearing) syllable of the word is stressed; if no heavy syllable, the first syllable; short toneless prefixes push stress rightward to the first heavy syllable; prefix ha~/ha- exceptionally always stressed (p. c. line 3451); two tones (high/low) on heavy syllables. NOTE: describes Bulu = Western Puroik (west2873/bulu1255), which the author states is not mutually intelligible with the eastern (Chayangtajo) varieties = sulu1241.

sources.note: Sec. 2.4 'Sulong', p. 80 (scanned of image-only PDF): 'On top of all these Sulong has developed a rudimentary system of tones, ignored completely in Tayeng's manual. The basic contrast seems to be between two pitch registers, mid level (varying with high level) versus low level. A further falling tone is recognized by Ouyang, but seems to be predictably associated with the glottal codas.' Nothing on stress. Second-hand: based on the ZMYYC (Sun Hongkai et al. 1991) record of the Longzi County (Tibet) variety = Eastern Puroik.
